newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: HOWARD TELLS PARLIAMENT HE "SIMPLY FORGOT" WOODS BRIEFING The Prime Minister has told parliament he did not set out to mislead the public over when he first learnt Liberal Senator Bob Woods was being investigated by Federal Police.
Mr Howard has revealed he was first briefed about the investigation late last year, after earlier saying he first heard of the investigation less than a fortnight ago.
Mr Howard has told parliament he simply forgot about the 1996 briefing and sought to clarify the matter as quickly as possible when he realised his error.
NO CHOCOLATE BAR OR FILM OFFERS SO FAR, SAYS BULLIMORE
British lone yachtsman Tony Bullimore arrived in Canberra today to meet his rescue co-ordinators before his return to Britain tomorrow.
He says he's received 8000 get-well letters since his rescue in the Southern Ocean but none have mentioned film offers or chocolate endorsements as has been rumoured.
Mr Bullimore is still in a wheelchair because of frost-bitten feet but says that his health has improved so much during his three-week recuperation that he intends to resume sailing in May.
DONATED $100,000 KEPT IN CALICO BAG: BURKE TRIAL
The District Court in Perth has been told former West Australian Premier Brian Burke kept cash given as donations to the Labor Party in a calico bag in his office safe.
Forty-nine-year-old Mr Burke is on trial accused of stealing between A$70,000 and A$100,000 from the Labor Party to buy stamps for his personal collection.
Mr Burke has pleaded not guilty.
Prosecutor Brian Martin told the Court today Mr Burke had requested that $100,000 of a $300,000 donation from a company associated with Yosse Goldberg be paid in cash.
Mr Martin said the money had been kept in a safe in Mr Burke's office and was used to purchase more than $85,000 worth of stamps.
The Court heard that Mr Burke told police later those stamps had been bought as an investment for the ALP.
Mr Burke also said he used to invest party funds in gold, real estate and the short term money market, as well as stamps.
The trial is continuing.
WAITING OVER AS TOP ARTS JOBS FILLED
Two of the nation's most keenly-sought Arts jobs have been filled. The Adelaide Festival's new general manager is Nicholas Hayward.
He's currently the chief executive officer of the Brisbane Biennial Music Festival and has held senior positions with Musica Viva and the Victorian Opera.
And ABC Chairman Donald McDonald will also become chairman of the Ring Corporation, which is staging the first southern hemisphere production of Wagner's Ring Cycle in November next year.
CARR DISTANCES NSW FROM OTHER STATES ON NATIVE TITLE ISSUE
The New South Wales Government is working on its own response to the Wik High Court judgement, and has distanced itself from a position put to the Prime Minister by other states.
The Premier, Bob Carr, says he's told his West Australian counterpart, Richard Court, NSW won't be a party to his proposal, despite apparent support from other states.
The proposal is reported to entail legislation that extinguishes native title, and a Year 2000 deadline for the lodgement of claims.
Mr Carr says he'd like an option that doesn't extinguish native title, but doesn't rule out legislation.
COPYRIGHT BREACH OVER OLYMPIC LOGO ALLEGED
The Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games is being accused in the Federal Court of breaching copyright over a logo for the sporting event.
Four sisters involved in the Sydney graphic design firm, Leuver, Leuver, Leuver and Leuver, have taken SOCOG to the Federal Court, alleging unfair, misleading conduct and breach of conduct.
The firm alleges its "boomerang man concept", which it submitted to a SOCOG logo competition in 1995, closely resembled the winning design.
The sisters are seeking credit for their work as well as damages for loss of opportunity and future income.
